To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the subunits of eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1H complex are overexpressed in non-small cell lung cancer and the subunits can exist as independent proteins in cancer cells.
the subunits of the eEF-1 complex are independently overexpressed in the human non small-cell lung cancer and some of them may function in the nucleus.
the subunits of the translation elongation factor eEF1H are overexpressed in human lung cancers and that some of them may play independent regulatory role.
In summary, our research is concerned with
novel mechanisms of the regulation of translation apparatus in cancer.
the novel mechanisms of cancer development and the role of eEF1 complex in the cancer progression.
the possibility of the existence of independent functions for some components of eEF1 complex in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the eEF1A/eEF1B interaction is lost in the A549 cell nuclei and that eEF1B is a nuclear factor that is not involved in protein synthesis.
eEF1H is not a stable complex but rather a dynamic structure, which is not necessarily present as a single complex in the cancer cells.
the eEF1 complex in cancer cells is not a stable complex, and its subunits may be present in the cell as independent units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the subunits of eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1 complex are overexpressed in human lung cancer and the subunits can act in a coordinated and independent manner.
the eEF1A, which is the most abundant subunit of eIF1B, can be released from the eEF1 complex in cancer cells and can play a novel role in tumor development.
the eEF1A-eEF1B interaction may be lost in cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subunits of eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1 complex eEF1 can exist in the cell as independent units and play non-translational roles.
the individual eEFH subunits can be used as independent markers of cancer.
the eEF1A subunit of eIF4F complex is not a unique case of the subunit dissociation and that the subunits of eIF4G complex are not obligatory components of eIF4E-eIF4G-eIF4A-eIF4B complex.
